findings.title: unsubscribe mutates notification state on an idempotent-unsafe GET
findings.body: topics#unsubscribe is wired to plain GET routes (config/routes.rb adds get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" and "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe") and it permanently writes the user's topic notification level before rendering the page. GET requests must not mutate state, and this one is not even idempotent: the first visit drops a watching/tracking user to regular, but simply reloading the confirmation page (or hitting back) executes the URL again and, because the level is now regular, falls into the else branch and fully mutes the topic — while the page still only claims 'You will stop receiving notifications'. It is also CSRF-able: any third-party page can embed and silently change a logged-in visitor's notification state, and any logged-in link prefetcher triggers it. The state change should happen via POST (the unsubscribe page already renders a topic-notifications-button the user can click), or the GET should render a confirmation without writing.

findings.title: NoMethodError (500) when the visitor has no TopicUser row
findings.body: tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) can return nil. Emailed users normally have a row because send_notification_email calls TopicUser.change, but the unsubscribe URL is reachable by any logged-in user — someone who never interacted with the topic, or whose topic_users row was later removed — and the very next line calls tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page. Guard the nil case or use TopicUser.change, which upserts.

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping, allowing silent re-subscription
findings.body: Assigning tu.notification_level and calling tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id are not updated and the notification_level_change MessageBus event is never published. One concrete consequence: TopicUser.update_last_read and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-subscribe users whose notifications_reason_id is null, and TopicUser.change would have stamped the reason as user_changed — because this code doesn't, a user who unsubscribes (set to regular) and later spends time reading the topic can be silently flipped back to tracking by the auto-track-on-view-time logic. Open browser tabs also won't reflect the new level in real time. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other add_unsubscribe_link callers
findings.body: The unsubscribe_link site text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})'), but Email::MessageBuilder only provides unsubscribe_url when the caller passes it in opts. The in-tree caller in user_notifications was updated, but any other caller of build_email with add_unsubscribe_link: true that doesn't pass unsubscribe_url (plugins, custom mailers) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building both the text body (MessageBuilder#body) and the HTML part (MessageBuilder#html_part), failing those emails entirely — the existing spec had to be changed for exactly this reason. Consider defaulting unsubscribe_url (e.g., to user_preferences_url) or making the second sentence conditional.

findings.title: No specs for the new state-mutating topics#unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a new endpoint that mutates user state with several branches — watching/tracking → regular, regular/muted → muted, missing TopicUser row, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, login requirement — but adds no controller or request specs for it; the only spec change passes unsubscribe_url in message_builder_spec. Even basic coverage would have caught the nil-TopicUser 500 and the non-idempotent escalation to muted on repeat visits described above.
